For he is judged not to set out that position fittingly and fully enough, and he argues against the words rather than against the mind of those who hold it. For that position does not mean that the appearing of the rainbow is a purely natural sign, and of itself a necessary one, that a flood will never come; but it is called a natural sign of that thing in this respect, that by its nature it shows that a flood is not soon to come, whereby it has a natural fitness for signifying, by God's good pleasure, that a flood will never come. Nor is this position contradicted by a third and clearer one, which says that the rainbow is a sign at will that there will be no flood, inasmuch as God of His good pleasure so ordained and willed that the appearing of this natural effect, namely the rainbow, should be a sign calling to mind the covenant God made with men that there would be no flood, or a sign that a flood will never come: as sometimes a stone lying in a field becomes, by men's good pleasure, a sign of the division of inheritances or of lordships. And this position was brought forward by Rabbi Moses Gerundensis [that is, Moses of Gerona, Nahmanides], and Saint Thomas too approves it in a certain place. Nor is it unfitting that a natural effect should be a sign at will of a supernatural or voluntary thing, which it cannot signify by nature.

paras.t: Erant ergo filii Noe, qui egressi sunt de arca, Sem, Cham, et Japhet. Porro Cham ipse est pater Chanaan. Sequenti capitulo legitur Cham filius Noe multos genuisse, inter quos Chanaan ultimus ponitur. Quare ergo nunc solus exprimitur, et specialiter filius Cham vocatur? Respondetur, quia de Chananæis ex Chanaan ortis intendebat Moyses plura conscribere, qualiter scilicet eorum terra data sit filiis Israel ; et quoniam Chanaan mores patris sui perversos creditur magis esse secutus, sicut et posteri Chanaan hujus. Tres isti filii sunt Noe, videlicet Sem, Cham, et Japhet. Dicit autem Hieronymus : Septuaginta sæpe non valentes HETH litteram Hebræam, quia duplicem sonat adspirationem, in Græcum vertere, addiderunt Z litteram Græcam, docentes in hujusmodi vocabulis adspirandum. Unde transtulerunt Cham, pro eo quod est Ham, a quo Ægyptus usque hodie lingua eorum vocatur Ham. Et ab his disseminatum est omne genus hominum super universam terram, id est, universi homines in toto mundo propagati sunt a præfatis filiis Noe.
paras.en: [[9:18|And the sons of Noe, who came out of the ark, were Sem, Cham, and Japheth: and Cham is the father of Chanaan|Erant ergo filii Noe, qui egressi sunt de arca, Sem, Cham, et Japhet. Porro Cham ipse est pater Chanaan]]. In the following chapter we read that Cham the son of Noe begot many, among whom Chanaan is put last. Why then is he alone named now, and called in particular the son of Cham? The answer is: because Moses meant to write a good deal about the Chanaanites who sprang from Chanaan, namely how their land was given to the children of Israel[[Jos 16:10||]]; and because Chanaan is believed to have followed his father's perverse ways more closely, as did the descendants of this Chanaan too. [[9:19|These three are the sons of Noe|Tres isti filii sunt Noe]], namely Sem, Cham, and Japheth. Now Jerome says: The Seventy, often unable to render the Hebrew letter HETH in Greek, because it sounds a double aspiration, added the Greek letter Z [so the print; Jerome means the Greek letter chi, χ], teaching that in words of this kind the aspiration is to be sounded. Hence they rendered Cham for what is Ham, from whom Egypt is called Ham in their tongue to this day; [[9:19|and from these was all mankind spread over the whole earth|Et ab his disseminatum est omne genus hominum super universam terram]]: that is, all men throughout the whole world were propagated from the aforesaid sons of Noe.

paras.t: Cœpit autem Noe vir agricola, cur Noe vocatus sit agricola, dictum est plenius circa finem expositionis quinti capituli, exercere terram, quod etiam aliqualiter fecit ante diluvium, sicut præhabitum est. Et plantavit vineam. Aliqui dicunt, quod vinea ista jam creverat, atque a Deo producta exstiterat, et plantata seu radicata in terra. Noe tamen dicitur eam plantasse, quia silvestris et dimissa fuerat vinea illa, ideo diligentius coluit illam. Porro in Scholastica historia legitur : Noe plantavit vineam, labruscas naturales trahens per cultum ad vineæ usum. Dicitur autem labrusca, a labrum, quod est labium animalium, quoniam labris eorum appendet atque exponitur dum ea pascuntur. Vel, quia in labris, id est extremitatibus viarum solent nasci. Bibensque vinum, inebriatus est: non enim expertus fuerat ante vim vini, nec ante diluvium exstitit usus vini, ut dicitur, et Alcuinus insinuat; et nudatus in tabernaculo suo, id est in sinu et verecundiæ loco, ubi generativa vis quasi in tabernaculo demoratur.
paras.en: [[9:20|And Noe a husbandman began|Cœpit autem Noe vir agricola]] (why Noe was called a husbandman was said more fully near the end of the exposition of the fifth chapter) [[9:20|to till the ground|exercere terram]], which he had also done in some measure before the flood, as was said earlier; [[9:20|and planted a vineyard|Et plantavit vineam]]. Some say that this vine had already grown, having been brought forth by God and planted, or rooted, in the earth; yet Noe is said to have planted it because that vine had been wild and left untended, and so he tended it with greater care. Further, in the Scholastic History we read: Noe planted a vineyard, bringing the natural wild vines [*labruscas*] by cultivation to the use of a vineyard. Now *labrusca* is so called from *labrum*, which is the lip of animals, because it hangs at their lips and lies open to them while they graze. Or because they commonly grow at the *labra*, that is, the edges, of the roads. [[9:21|And drinking of the wine was made drunk|Bibensque vinum, inebriatus est]]: for he had not experienced the strength of wine before, nor was there any use of wine before the flood, as is said, and as Alcuin implies; [[9:21|and was uncovered in his tent|et nudatus in tabernaculo suo]], that is, in the lap, the place of shame, where the generative power abides as it were in a tent.

paras.t: Quod quum vidisset Cham pater Chanaan, verenda patris sui esse nudata. Ex quo elicitur, quod homines tunc usque femoralibus non utebantur. Et si dicatur, quod forte deposuit ea, dicendum quod non deposuisset ea in die, et quando adhuc bibebat. Dicuntque aliqui, quod mulier nomine Semiramis, invenit postmodum femoralium formationem et usum. Alibi legitur, quod Minerva quæ vocabatur dea sapientiæ, invenit usum lini ac olei et femoralium, nisi forte sit eadem mulier pluribus designata nominibus. Nuntiavit duobus fratribus suis foras, ut secum deriderent proprium patrem, tanquam inhonestum et turpiter se habentem. At vero Sem et Japhet pallium imposuerunt humeris suis, et incedentes retrorsum, operuerunt verenda patris sui ; faciesque eorum aversæ erant, et patris virilia non viderunt. In quo patet caritas, reverentia, et pudicitia ipsorum ad patrem suum.
paras.en: [[9:22|Which when Cham the father of Chanaan had seen|Quod quum vidisset Cham pater Chanaan]], [[9:22|that his father's nakedness was uncovered|verenda patris sui esse nudata]]. From this it is gathered that men at that time did not yet use breeches. And if it be said that perhaps he had taken them off, the answer is that he would not have taken them off by day, and while he was still drinking. And some say that a woman named Semiramis afterwards invented the making and use of breeches. Elsewhere we read that Minerva, who was called the goddess of wisdom, invented the use of flax and of oil and of breeches; unless perhaps it is the same woman, designated by several names. [[9:22|he told it to his two brethren without|Nuntiavit duobus fratribus suis foras]], so that they might deride their own father along with him, as one indecent and behaving shamefully. [[9:23|But Sem and Japheth put a cloak upon their shoulders, and going backward, covered the nakedness of their father: and their faces were turned away, and they saw not their father's nakedness.|At vero Sem et Japhet pallium imposuerunt humeris suis, et incedentes retrorsum, operuerunt verenda patris sui ; faciesque eorum aversæ erant, et patris virilia non viderunt]] In this their charity, reverence and modesty toward their father are plain.

paras.t: Evigilans autem Noe ex vino, id est ex somno quem ex immoderata vini potatione incurrit, quum didicisset, vel ex revelatione humana, vel ex revelatione divina seu spiritu prophetali, ut Glossa interlinearis videtur innuere, quæ fecerat ei filius suus minor, videlicet Cham, qui etsi non fuerit ultimus natu, fuit tamen minor virtute et gratia, et per consequens vilior ac indignior. Vel minor forsan statura, aut minor primogenito: sicque ultimo natus, minimus dici posset, secundum quod infra filii Jacob dixerunt de Benjamin: Minimus cum patre est. Quidam tamen per minorem istum, intelligunt Japhet, ita quod Noe cognovit quod Japhet junior fratribus suis, habuit se magis reverenter ac sapienter circa patrem suum, quam Cham senior eo. Ait: Maledictus puer Chanaan, servus servorum erit fratribus suis. Refert quidam, quod aliqui dicunt Chanaan filium Cham, maledici a Noe, quoniam primo vidit virilia Noe avi sui, et retulit patri suo Cham se ea vidisse. Sicque incepit crimen illius derisionis a Chanaan. Sed istud videtur ineptum. Nullus enim trium filiorum Noe genuit ante diluvium, sed postea. Plantatio autem vineæ facta a Noe, videtur contigisse post diluvium satis cito, ut textus insinuare censetur. Statim etenim post diluvium concessus est a Deo hominibus usus vini, quemadmodum carnium eisdem ex causis. Ergo Chanaan fuit tunc juvenis multum. Propter quod in littera puer vocatur.
paras.en: [[9:24|And Noe awaking from the wine|Evigilans autem Noe ex vino]], that is, from the sleep into which he fell through immoderate drinking of wine, [[9:24|when he had learned|quum didicisset]], whether by human report or by divine revelation, that is, by the spirit of prophecy, as the interlinear Gloss seems to imply, [[9:24|what his younger son had done to him|quæ fecerat ei filius suus minor]], namely Cham: who, though he was not the last born, was yet the less [*minor*, which means both "younger" and "less"] in virtue and grace, and consequently the baser and more unworthy. Or perhaps less in stature, or younger than the firstborn; and so one born last could be called the least, as below the sons of Jacob said of Benjamin: [[Gen 42:13|the youngest is with our father|Minimus cum patre est]] [the margin's chapter number is lost; the words are those of Gen 42:13, said again at 42:32]. Some, however, understand by this younger son Japheth: so that Noe learned that Japheth, younger than his brothers, had borne himself more reverently and wisely toward his father than Cham, who was older than he. [[9:25|He said: Cursed be Chanaan|Ait: Maledictus puer Chanaan]] [Denis reads *Maledictus puer Chanaan*, "Cursed be the boy Chanaan": the word *puer*, "boy", which he takes up below, is not in the Clementine text], [[9:25|a servant of servants shall he be unto his brethren|servus servorum erit fratribus suis]]. A certain writer relates that some say Chanaan the son of Cham was cursed by Noe because he first saw the nakedness of Noe his grandfather and told his father Cham that he had seen it; and so the crime of that mockery began with Chanaan. But this seems unfitting. For none of the three sons of Noe begot children before the flood, but afterwards; and the planting of the vineyard by Noe seems to have happened quite soon after the flood, as the text is thought to imply. For straight after the flood the use of wine was granted by God to men, as was that of flesh, for the same reasons. Therefore Chanaan was at that time very young. That is why in the text he is called a boy.

paras.t: Verumtamen tunc quæstio oritur, cur propter patris peccatum maledicitur filius, quum alibi scriptum sit. Filius non portabit iniquitatem patris. Respondetur, quod pater maledicitur in filio suo, et per filium suum. Deus enim visitat iniquitatem patrum in filios usque in tertiam et quartam generationem. Quum equidem filius sit aliquid sui patris, utpote ex ejus substantia natus, quantum ad corpus: potest juste, quantum ad corporalia quædam mala pœnalia, puniri pro parentum peccato; non autem quantum ad animam, ita ut spiritualia dona gratiæ ac virtutum, filiis subtrahantur propter culpam parentum. Animam quippe habet filius, non a parentibus, sed immediate a Deo. Hæc autem maledictio Chanaan fuit quoddam malum pœnæ temporalis, videlicet servitus corporalis, quæ nec in Cham, nec in filio ejus Chanaan, sed diu post in Chananæis impleta est, qui filiis Israel ex Sem natis, fuerunt diu omnino subjecti. Nec hoc fuit injustum, quoniam Chananæi illi iniquitatem Cham et filii ejus Chanaan sunt secuti, et multo majora commiserunt peccata: quemadmodum Judæi usque in præsens pro Christi occisione in miseriis detinentur, quoniam patrum suorum qui Christum occiderunt, impietatem perfidiamque sequuntur. Pœna vero filiorum redundat in patres. Hinc Strabus ait: Chananæi a Chanaan orti, hac maledictione prophetantur expellendi et subjiciendi. Et idem habetur in Glossa. Itaque, Maledictus Chanaan, hoc est temporalibus pœnis addictus, juxta sensum inductum, servus servorum, id est servus maxime subditus, erit fratribus suis. Porro Cham patrem suum sic subsannando, peccavit mortaliter, et pœnam meruit infernalem: quam tamen pater ejus ei imprecari non voluit, nec prænuntiare; temporalem vero pœnam posteritati prædixit, quoniam talis pœna est medicinalis.
paras.en: But here a question arises: why is the son cursed for the father's sin, when it is written elsewhere: [[Ezech 18:20|the son shall not bear the iniquity of the father|Filius non portabit iniquitatem patris]]? The answer is that the father is cursed in his son and through his son. For God is the God [[Ex 20:5|visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children, unto the third and fourth generation|visitat iniquitatem patrum in filios usque in tertiam et quartam generationem]][[Num 14:18||]]. Since indeed the son is something of his father, being born of his substance as regards the body, he can justly be punished for his parents' sin as regards certain bodily penal evils; but not as regards the soul, so that the spiritual gifts of grace and of the virtues should be withdrawn from the children for the fault of the parents. For the son has his soul not from his parents but immediately from God. Now this curse of Chanaan was a certain evil of temporal punishment, namely bodily servitude, which was fulfilled neither in Cham nor in his son Chanaan, but long afterwards in the Chanaanites, who were for a long time wholly subject to the children of Israel, born of Sem. Nor was this unjust, since those Chanaanites followed the iniquity of Cham and of his son Chanaan, and committed far greater sins: just as the Jews are held in miseries to this present day for the slaying of Christ, because they follow the impiety and faithlessness of their fathers who slew Christ. And the punishment of the sons redounds upon the fathers. Hence Strabo says: The Chanaanites, sprung from Chanaan, are foretold by this curse as to be driven out and subjected. And the same is found in the Gloss. And so: [[9:25|Cursed be Chanaan|Maledictus Chanaan]], that is, given over to temporal punishments, according to the sense set out; [[9:25|a servant of servants|servus servorum]], that is, a servant most thoroughly subject, [[9:25|shall he be unto his brethren|erit fratribus suis]]. Cham, moreover, by mocking his father in this way, sinned mortally and deserved the punishment of hell: which yet his father would not call down upon him, nor foretell; but he foretold a temporal punishment for his posterity, since such punishment is medicinal.

paras.t: Circa quod quæri potest, cur Noe vir justus, pius, et patiens, maledixit sic posteris suis. Respondetur, quod fecit hoc non rancore aut vitio, sed justitiæ zelo, imo ex caritate, ut per temporalia corrigerentur adversa. Et magis fuit prophetica prænuntiatio, quam mali imprecatio: atque ut in Scholastica fertur historia, iste est sensus: Maledictus Chanaan puer, hoc est, tu Cham non læteris de filio tuo, sicut nec ego de te.
paras.en: On this it may be asked why Noe, a just, devout and patient man, thus cursed his descendants. The answer is that he did this not out of rancour or vice, but out of zeal for justice, indeed out of charity, that they might be corrected through temporal adversities. And it was a prophetic foretelling rather than an imprecation of evil; and, as is said in the Scholastic History, this is the sense: [[9:25|Cursed be Chanaan|Maledictus Chanaan]] the boy: that is, Thou, Cham, shalt not rejoice in thy son, as neither do I in thee.

paras.t: Dixitque Noe: Benedictus Dominus Deus Sem, id est, sit Deus laudatus et glorificatus pro donis gratiæ, quæ daturus est Sem et posteris ejus. Hoc dixit, quia prævidit in spiritu quod in posteris Sem, scilicet filiis Israel, permansurus erat cultus Dei, aliis ad idolorum culturam ruentibus : sitque Chanaan servus ejus, id est, posteritas Chanaan serviat posteritati Sem, sicut ostensum est.
paras.en: [[9:26|And he said|Dixitque]] Noe: [[9:26|Blessed be the Lord God of Sem|Benedictus Dominus Deus Sem]]: that is, may God be praised and glorified for the gifts of grace which He is to give to Sem and to his descendants. He said this because he foresaw in spirit that among the descendants of Sem, namely the children of Israel, the worship of God would endure, while the others rushed into the worship of idols; [[9:26|be Chanaan his servant|sitque Chanaan servus ejus]]: that is, may the posterity of Chanaan serve the posterity of Sem, as has been shown.

paras.t: Dilatet Deus Japhet, id est, semen ejus multiplicet : quod impletum est in gentibus multis ex semine Japhet natis, ut sequenti patebit capitulo. Et habitet in tabernaculis Sem. Istud secundum Hieronymum, impletum est in conversis ex gentilitate, qui ejectis et reprobatis Judæis incredulis, habitaverunt in terra promissionis, seu potius in spiritualibus bonis, videlicet in scientia Scripturarum veteris Testamenti, versantur, et in Ecclesia Dei, in qua ante erant filii Sem. In veteri quoque Testamento quidam gentiles ex Japhet orti, ad Judaismum convertebantur. Sitque Chanaan servus ejus, id est, etiam posteritati ipsius Japhet famuletur posteritas Chanaan. Gentiles quippe conversi, dominati sunt copiose et sæpe incredulis gentibus.
paras.en: [[9:27|May God enlarge Japheth|Dilatet Deus Japhet]]: that is, may He multiply his seed: which was fulfilled in the many nations born of the seed of Japheth, as will appear in the following chapter; [[9:27|and may he dwell in the tents of Sem|Et habitet in tabernaculis Sem]]. This, according to Jerome, was fulfilled in those converted from among the Gentiles, who, when the unbelieving Jews had been cast out and rejected, dwelt in the land of promise, or rather abide in spiritual goods, namely in the knowledge of the Scriptures of the Old Testament, and in the Church of God, in which the sons of Sem were before them. In the Old Testament too some Gentiles sprung from Japheth were converted to Judaism; [[9:27|and Chanaan be his servant|Sitque Chanaan servus ejus]]: that is, may the posterity of Chanaan serve the posterity of Japheth also. For the converted Gentiles have often ruled far and wide over unbelieving nations.

paras.t: Itaque sicut Noe maledixit Cham et posteris ejus, propter irreverentiam et ingratitudinem ac derisionem suam in patrem suum, sic benedixit filiis suis Sem et Japhet, eorumque posteris, propter benevolentiam et reverentiam ipsorum in se patrem eorum. Ex quibus etiam patet, quam grandi gratia prophetiæ fuerit decoratus.
paras.en: And so, as Noe cursed Cham and his descendants for his irreverence and ingratitude and his mockery of his father, so he blessed his sons Sem and Japheth and their descendants for their goodwill and reverence toward himself, their father. From which it is also plain with how great a grace of prophecy he was adorned.

paras.t: Vixit autem Noe post diluvium trecentis quinquaginta annis, et impleti sunt omnes dies ejus nongentorum quinquaginta annorum, et mortuus est. Sicque post diluvium nullus pervenit ad ejus ætatem, nec ante diluvium aliquis fuit senior, dempto Mathusalem, qui decem et novem annis diutius vixit. Dempto quoque Jared, qui vixit annis nongentis sexaginta duobus.
paras.en: [[9:28|And Noe lived after the flood three hundred and fifty years.|Vixit autem Noe post diluvium trecentis quinquaginta annis]] [[9:29|And all his days were in the whole nine hundred and fifty years: and he died.|et impleti sunt omnes dies ejus nongentorum quinquaginta annorum, et mortuus est]] And so after the flood no one reached his age, nor before the flood was anyone older, except Mathusala, who lived nineteen years longer; and except also Jared, who lived nine hundred and sixty-two years.

paras.t: Circa prædicta quæritur, an Noe post diluvium genuit aliquam prolem, ex qua nati sunt alii. Et apparet quod non, quia in isto capitulo clarissime dictum est, quod ex his tribus filiis Noe, videlicet Sem, Cham, et Japhet, disseminatum est omne genus hominum super universam terram. Quod etiam Augustinus, aliique doctores concorditer asserunt. Oppositum vero videtur, auctoritate Methodii martyris, qui in libello suo apertissime scribit, quod centesimo anno tertiæ chiliadis, hoc est, tertii millenarii a principio mundi, Noe genuit filium nomine Jonitum. Et de filio isto ejusque regno, multa scribit Methodius, asserens eum accepisse a Deo sapientiæ donum, et invenisse astronomiam. Denique auctor Scholasticæ historiæ ista quasi vera allegat, et multa de Jonito isto prosequitur. Et natus est Jonitus secundum istos, egresso Noe de arca. Alioqui fuisset in arca. Ad istud breviter respondendo, fateor me nescire, nec posse perpendere, qualiter ista narratio de Jonito possit cum Scriptura ista canonica concordari. Et si vera esset, mirum valde quod Moyses nihil tetigisset de ea, quum tanta consequenter scribat de rebus multo minoribus, et generationibus filiorum Noe, ostendens ex eis ceteros omnes posteriores esse exortos : ideo nolo incerta certis præponere, nec derogare auctoritati Scripturæ canonicæ, propter ea quæ minoris aut parvæ seu nullius sunt auctoritatis. Porro qui narrationem illam de Jonito vult salvare, ad ista respondeat.
paras.en: On the foregoing it is asked whether Noe after the flood begot any offspring from whom others were born. And it appears not, since it is said most clearly in this chapter that from these three sons of Noe, namely Sem, Cham and Japheth, [[9:19|was all mankind spread over the whole earth|disseminatum est omne genus hominum super universam terram]]; which Augustine also and other doctors assert with one accord. But the opposite seems to follow from the authority of Methodius the martyr, who writes most openly in his little book that in the hundredth year of the third chiliad, that is, of the third thousand years from the beginning of the world, Noe begot a son named Jonitus. And about this son and his kingdom Methodius writes much, asserting that he received from God the gift of wisdom and invented astronomy. Further, the author of the Scholastic History cites these things as though true, and relates much about this Jonitus. And according to them Jonitus was born after Noe had come out of the ark; otherwise he would have been in the ark. Answering this briefly, I confess that I do not know, nor can I weigh out, how this account of Jonitus can be reconciled with this canonical Scripture. And if it were true, it is very strange that Moses should have touched on nothing of it, since in what follows he writes so much about far lesser matters, and about the generations of the sons of Noe, showing that all others after them sprang from them. Therefore I will not set uncertain things before certain ones, nor derogate from the authority of canonical Scripture for the sake of things of lesser or slight or no authority. Whoever, then, wishes to save that account of Jonitus, let him answer these points.

9.title: Spiritualis expositio ejusdem capituli noni
9.title_en: Spiritual exposition of the same ninth chapter

paras.t: Benedixitque Deus Noe et filios ejus. Post Christi passionem et resurrectionem, Deus Pater seu Trinitas Deus, Christo homini benedixit, eum glorificando, quantum ad humanitatem assumptam. Benedixit etiam ei, per evangelicam prædicationem eum ubique laudando, et per diversa miracula exaltando. Filiis vero ejus (puta discipulis) benedixit, variarum gratiarum charismata conferendo eisdem. Et dixit ad eos: Crescite et multiplicamini, alios convertendo ad fidem, spiritualesque filios generando. Crescite quoque, proficiendo in omni gratia ac virtute, quod tamen Christo non competebat, nisi secundum exteriorem manifestationem. Unde in Evangelio legitur: Jesus proficiebat sapientia, ætate, et gratia. Et replete terram fidelibus. Dilataverunt enim sancti Apostoli Ecclesiam Christi per omnia climata mundi.
paras.en: [[9:1|And God blessed Noe and his sons|Benedixitque Deus Noe et filios ejus]]. After the passion and resurrection of Christ, God the Father, or God the Trinity, blessed Christ the man by glorifying him as to the humanity he had assumed. He blessed him also by praising him everywhere through the preaching of the Gospel, and by exalting him through various miracles. And he blessed his sons (that is, the disciples) by bestowing on them the gifts of various graces. [[9:1|And he said to them: Increase, and multiply|Et dixit ad eos: Crescite et multiplicamini]], by converting others to the faith and begetting spiritual sons. Increase also by advancing in every grace and virtue; which yet did not belong to Christ except as to its outward showing. Hence we read in the Gospel: [[Luke 2:52|Jesus advanced in wisdom and age and grace|Jesus proficiebat sapientia, ætate, et gratia]]. [[9:1|and fill the earth|Et replete terram]] with the faithful. For the holy Apostles spread the Church of Christ through every region of the world.

paras.t: Et terror ac tremor vester sit super cuncta animalia terræ, et super omnes volucres cæli, hoc est, universi qui convertuntur ad fidem, sive per animalia terrestria, sive per volatilia designentur, propter proprietatum suarum diversitates, timeant vos ac formident. Deus quippe constituit sanctos Apostolos principes super omnem terram. Subditi autem habent prælatos suos diligere ac timere. Omnes pisces maris manui vestræ traditi sunt. Per pisces maris, intelliguntur lascivi, qui in aquis concupiscentiæ volutantur: vel prudentes sæculi, qui in humanæ sapientiæ abundantia, quasi aquis natant: sive hæretici, quibus aquæ furtivæ et propriæ et separatæ doctrinæ, sunt dulciores quam aquæ sapientiæ salutaris Catholicorum. Omnes isti traditi sunt manui Apostolorum discipulorumque Christi; tum quoniam multos et ex eorum genere talium hominum converterunt; tum quoniam omnibus illis per sapientiam desuper eis infusam prævaluerunt, sicut Christus prædixit: Dabo vobis os et sapientiam, cui non poterunt resistere omnes adversarii vestri.
paras.en: [[9:2|let the fear and dread of you be upon all the beasts of the earth, and upon all the fowls of the air|Et terror ac tremor vester sit super cuncta animalia terræ, et super omnes volucres cæli]]: that is, let all who are converted to the faith, whether they are signified by the beasts of the earth or by the birds, according to the diversity of their properties, fear and dread you. For God appointed the holy Apostles [[Ps 44:17|princes over all the earth|principes super omnem terram]] [the margin gives Ps. xlvi, 17; the words are those of Ps 44:17]. And subjects are bound to love and fear their prelates. [[9:2|all the fishes of the sea are delivered into your hand|Omnes pisces maris manui vestræ traditi sunt]]. By the fishes of the sea are understood the wanton, who wallow in the waters of concupiscence; or the prudent of the world, who swim in the abundance of human wisdom as in waters; or heretics, to whom the [[Prov 9:17|Stolen waters|aquæ furtivæ]] of their own separate doctrine are [[Prov 9:17|sweeter|dulciores]] than the waters of the saving wisdom of the Catholics. All these are delivered into the hand of the Apostles and disciples of Christ: both because they converted many, even of the kind of such men, and because they prevailed over all of them by the wisdom poured into them from above, as Christ foretold: [[Luke 21:15|I will give you a mouth and wisdom, which all your adversaries shall not be able to resist|Dabo vobis os et sapientiam, cui non poterunt resistere omnes adversarii vestri]].

paras.t: Et omne quod movetur et vivit, erit vobis in cibum: id est, de conversione universorum hominum spiritualiter reficiemini, et quosdam, imo et plurimos, de omni genere hominum incorporabitis Christo, et ex eis nutrietis Ecclesiam. Tales enim sunt nutritivæ Ecclesiæ partes, ex quibus quotidie alitur, augetur et impinguatur, easque in mysticum suum convertit ac trajicit corpus, propter quod, sicut in Actibus legitur, dictum est beatissimo Archiapostolo: Surge, Petre, occide et manduca. Quasi olera virentia tradidi vobis omnia. Per olera virentia, exprimuntur electi qui ex Judaismo conversi sunt, qui et antea in Synagoga floruerunt per notitiam legis et cultum unius Dei. Quemadmodum ergo tales Apostolis dati sunt in præfatam refectionem, conversionem et incorporationem, ita deinde Deus eis subjecit omnes gentes, tribus et linguas, quoniam, In omnem terram exivit sonus eorum, et in fines orbis terræ verba eorum, impletumque est quod Daniel prophetavit: Omnes populi, tribus et linguæ servient ei, videlicet Christo.
paras.en: [[9:3|And every thing that moveth, and liveth shall be meat for you|Et omne quod movetur et vivit, erit vobis in cibum]]: that is, you shall be spiritually refreshed by the conversion of all men, and some, indeed very many, of every kind of men you shall incorporate into Christ, and with them you shall nourish the Church. For such are the nourishing parts of the Church, by which she is daily fed, increased and fattened, and which she turns and passes over into her mystical body; for which reason, as we read in the Acts, it was said to the most blessed chief Apostle: [[Acts 10:13|Arise, Peter. Kill and eat|Surge, Petre, occide et manduca]]. [[9:3|even as the green herbs have I delivered them all to you|Quasi olera virentia tradidi vobis omnia]]. By the green herbs are signified the elect who were converted from Judaism, who even before had flourished in the Synagogue through knowledge of the law and the worship of the one God. As, then, such men were given to the Apostles for the refreshment, conversion and incorporation spoken of, so afterwards God subjected to them all nations, tribes and tongues, since [[Ps 18:5|Their sound hath gone forth into all the earth: and their words unto the ends of the world|In omnem terram exivit sonus eorum, et in fines orbis terræ verba eorum]]; and there was fulfilled what Daniel prophesied: [[Dan 7:14|all peoples, tribes, and tongues shall serve him|Omnes populi, tribus et linguæ servient ei]], that is, Christ.

paras.t: Excepto quod carnem cum sanguine non comedetis: id est, carnalia opera et peccata hominum prædictorum non acceptabitis, sed per confessionem effundi facietis ab eis, præcipiendo eisdem: Confitemini alterutrum peccata vestra.
paras.en: [[9:4|Saving that flesh with blood you shall not eat|Excepto quod carnem cum sanguine non comedetis]]: that is, you shall not accept the carnal works and sins of the men spoken of, but shall make them pour them out through confession, commanding them: [[Jas 5:16|Confess therefore your sins one to another|Confitemini alterutrum peccata vestra]].

paras.t: Sanguinem enim animarum vestrarum requiram de manu cunctarum bestiarum, et de manu hominis; de manu viri et de manu fratris ejus requiram animam hominis. Per hæc verba Deus prohibet, juxta mysticum sensum, spirituale homicidium, ne quis invidendo, loquendo, obloquendo, aut scandalizando proximum perimat, quod totum Deus districte ulciscitur. Nempe per sanguinem animarum seu hominis, designatur in hac auctoritate spiritualis vita, quæ est vita gratiæ et virtutis. Unde ad Ezechielem loquitur Deus de pereunte: Sanguinem ejus de manu tua requiram. Hinc subditur: Quicumque effuderit humanum sanguinem, hoc est, aliquem ad mortale peccatum induxerit, seu animam ejus spiritualiter occiderit, fundetur sanguis illius, id est, etiam ipse alium taliter scandalizando, peccat mortaliter et peribit.
paras.en: [[9:5|For I will require the blood of your lives at the hand of every beast, and at the hand of man, at the hand of every man, and of his brother, will I require the life of man|Sanguinem enim animarum vestrarum requiram de manu cunctarum bestiarum, et de manu hominis; de manu viri et de manu fratris ejus requiram animam hominis]]. By these words God forbids, according to the mystical sense, spiritual homicide: that no one should destroy his neighbour by envying, by talking, by detraction, or by scandalizing him [that is, by leading him into sin], all of which God strictly avenges. For by the blood of souls, or of man, is signified in this text the spiritual life, which is the life of grace and virtue. Hence God says to Ezechiel of one who perishes: [[Ezech 3:18|I will require his blood at thy hand|Sanguinem ejus de manu tua requiram]]. Then follows: [[9:6|Whosoever shall shed man's blood|Quicumque effuderit humanum sanguinem]], that is, whosoever has led another into mortal sin, or has killed his soul spiritually, [[9:6|his blood shall be shed|fundetur sanguis illius]]: that is, he too, by so scandalizing another, sins mortally and shall perish.

paras.t: Ecce ego statuam pactum meum vobiscum, et cum semine vestro, etc. Arcum meum ponam in nubibus, etc. Per arcum seu iridem, significatur Christi humanitas, ejusque passio: quæ humanitas tanquam arcus in passione extenta est, et rubeo colore rosei sanguinis sui perfusa, coloreque aqueo, dum aqua exivit de latere ejus transverberato. Hunc arcum ponit Deus in nubibus, id est in scripturis Prophetarum atque Apostolorum, in sermonibus quoque prædicatorum: qui arcus est signum pacis et fœderis inter Deum et homines, quoniam Christus per sanguinem crucis suæ pacificavit omnia, sive quæ in cœlis, sive quæ in terris sunt. Hunc arcum Deus Pater intuetur. Filius namque ostendit Patri latus et vulnera, idcirco Pater miseretur hominibus, nec aquas diluvii ultra inducit, hoc est, homines non relinquit, nec plagat ulterius, quemadmodum olim in lege naturali ac scripta.
paras.en: [[9:9|Behold I will establish my covenant with you, and with your seed|Ecce ego statuam pactum meum vobiscum, et cum semine vestro]], etc. [[9:13|I will set my bow in the clouds|Arcum meum ponam in nubibus]], etc. By the bow, or rainbow, is signified the humanity of Christ and his passion: which humanity was stretched out like a bow in the passion, and steeped in the red colour of his rosy blood, and in the colour of water when water came out of his pierced side[[John 19:34||]]. This bow God sets in the clouds, that is, in the writings of the Prophets and Apostles, and in the sermons of preachers too: and this bow is the sign of peace and of covenant between God and men, since Christ, [[Col 1:20|making peace through the blood of his cross|per sanguinem crucis suæ pacificavit]], has set at peace all things, [[Col 1:20|the things that are in heaven|sive quæ in cœlis]] as well as [[Col 1:20|the things that are on earth|sive quæ in terris sunt]]. This bow God the Father beholds. For the Son shows the Father his side and his wounds; and therefore the Father has mercy on men, and no longer brings on the waters of the flood: that is, he does not abandon men, nor strike them any more, as once in the law of nature and the written law.

paras.t: Tres isti filii sunt Noe, et ab his disseminatum est omne genus hominum super universam terram. Per Sem, qui interpretatur nominatus, designatur chorus Apostolorum, qui ceteris Christi discipulis excellentiores et famosiores fuerunt. Per Cham, qui interpretatur callidus, intelliguntur hæretici, qui in primitiva Ecclesia consurrexerunt adversus Catholicos pleni vulpina versutia, et humana aut naturali quadam scientia, seque Christi discipulos ac filios nominaverunt. Porro per Japhet, qui interpretatur latitudo, intelligitur ordo septuaginta duorum discipulorum, et aliorum primorum credentium. Ex quibus tribus propagati sunt ceteri Christiani, tam catholici, qui soli vere Christiani censentur: quam hæretici, qui se Christianos mendaciter appellarunt.
paras.en: [[9:19|These three are the sons of Noe: and from these was all mankind spread over the whole earth|Tres isti filii sunt Noe, et ab his disseminatum est omne genus hominum super universam terram]]. By Sem, which is interpreted "named," is signified the company of the Apostles, who were more excellent and more renowned than the other disciples of Christ. By Cham, which is interpreted "crafty," are understood the heretics, who in the early Church rose up against the Catholics, full of foxlike cunning and of a certain human or natural knowledge, and called themselves disciples and sons of Christ. And by Japhet, which is interpreted "breadth," is understood the order of the seventy-two disciples and of the other first believers. From these three the rest of Christians have been propagated: both the Catholics, who alone are held to be truly Christians, and the heretics, who have falsely called themselves Christians.

paras.t: Cœpit autem Noe vir agricola exercere terram. Christus vir est, de quo loquitur Jeremias: Novum faciet Dominus super terram, Mulier circumdabit virum. Ipse quoque agricola, qui corda humana vomere prædicationis salubriter fregit, semine verbi cœlestis fecundavit, et triticum, puta electos, in horreum suæ collegit Ecclesiæ. Nec obstat quod ait: Ego sum vitis vera, et Pater meus agricola est. Nam Christus, in quantum Deus, est idem cum Patre agricola: imo tota superdignissima Trinitas est unus agricola, sicut et unus creator. Nihilo minus Christus, secundum naturam humanam, agricola est quasi instrumentalis: nec solum ipse, sed ei prælati ejus vicarii, quum scriptum sit: Homo quidam paterfamilias plantavit vineam, et locavit eam agricolis. Porro Deus Trinitas est principalis agricola, qui solus per interiorem gratiæ infusionem, totiusque obicis potestativam remotionem, cordium cultor est. Cœpit autem Christus per se ipsum, factus homo, exercere terram, videlicet Synagogam, quæ terrena habebat promissa, prædicando Judæis. Et plantavit vineam, scilicet primitivam Ecclesiam, imo et Synagogam, secundum quod Deus, plantavit, de qua loquitur Isaias: Vinea Domini Sabaoth domus Israel est. Et Osee: Vitis frondosa Israel.
paras.en: [[9:20|Noe a husbandman began to till the ground|Cœpit autem Noe vir agricola exercere terram]]. Christ is the man [*vir*, the word used of Noe in the lemma, *vir agricola*] of whom Jeremias speaks: [[Jer 31:22|the Lord hath created a new thing upon the earth: A WOMAN SHALL COMPASS A MAN|Novum faciet Dominus super terram, Mulier circumdabit virum]]. He too is the husbandman who broke up human hearts for their health with the ploughshare of preaching, made them fruitful with the seed of the heavenly word, and gathered the wheat, that is, the elect, into the barn of his Church. Nor does it stand in the way that he says: [[John 15:1|I am the true vine: and my Father is the husbandman|Ego sum vitis vera, et Pater meus agricola est]]. For Christ, inasmuch as he is God, is one and the same husbandman with the Father: indeed the whole most exalted Trinity is one husbandman, as it is also one Creator. Nonetheless Christ, according to his human nature, is a husbandman as it were instrumentally [that is, as the instrument through which the Godhead works]; and not he alone, but also the prelates who are his vicars, since it is written: [[Matt 21:33|a man, an householder, who planted a vineyard|Homo quidam paterfamilias plantavit vineam]], [[Matt 21:33|and let it out to husbandmen|et locavit eam agricolis]]. But God the Trinity is the principal husbandman, who alone is the tiller of hearts, by the inward pouring in of grace and the removal, by his power, of every obstacle. And Christ began by himself, when he was made man, to till the ground, namely the Synagogue, which had earthly promises, by preaching to the Jews. [[9:20|and planted a vineyard|Et plantavit vineam]], that is, the early Church; indeed, as God, he planted the Synagogue too, of which Isaias says: [[Is 5:7|the vineyard of the Lord of hosts is the house of Israel|Vinea Domini Sabaoth domus Israel est]]. And Osee: [[Osee 10:1|Israel a vine full of branches|Vitis frondosa Israel]].

paras.t: Bibensque vinum, id est rigorem justitiæ et increpationis vigorem assumens, de quo vino testatur, quod Samaritanus infudit vulnerato vinum et oleum, inebriatus est, id est, caritatis fervore. Passionisque calice excessive repletus est usque ad summum, juxta illud Threnorum, Inebriavit me absinthio; et […] nudus enim in cruce suspensus est: et hoc, In tabernaculo suo, utpote in medio populi Synagogæ. Quod quum vidisset Cham pater Chanaan, id est incredulus populus Judæorum, pater infidelium posteriorum, […] […], hoc est, mortalitatem, humanasque carnis fragilitatem Christi creatoris sui patere ad oculum, nuntiavit duobus fratribus suis, id est, tam ceteros Judæos quam Gentiles, qui natura fratres eorum erant, provocavit ad Christi irrisionem, dicendo: Alios salvos fecit, se ipsum non potest salvum facere. Itemque: Commovit populum et seduxit. At vero Sem et Japhet pallium imposuerunt humeris suis: hoc est, conversi ad Christum ex Judaismo et paganismo, præfatam Christi nuditatem rationabiliter excusarunt, et defenderunt ab omni incredulorum aspernatione, dicentes Christum non necessitate, nec propria culpa, sed caritate et pro totius mundi salute incarnatum et crucifixum. Hinc secundum Augustinum, per pallium exprimitur sacramentum: per humeros, memoria præteritorum.
paras.en: [[9:21|And drinking of the wine|Bibensque vinum]], that is, taking up the rigour of justice and the vigour of rebuke: the wine of which it is testified that the Samaritan poured wine and oil into the wounded man[[Luke 10:34||]]; [[9:21|was made drunk|inebriatus est]], that is, with the fervour of charity. And he was filled beyond measure, to the very brim, with the chalice of the passion, according to that word of Lamentations: [[Lam 3:15|he hath inebriated me with wormwood|Inebriavit me absinthio]]; and […]: for he was hung naked on the cross; and this [[9:21|in his tent|In tabernaculo suo]], that is, in the midst of the people of the Synagogue. [[9:22|Which when Cham the father of Chanaan had seen|Quod quum vidisset Cham pater Chanaan]], that is, the unbelieving people of the Jews, the father of the unbelievers who came after, […] […], that is, the mortality and the frailty of the human flesh of Christ his Creator lying open to the eye, [[9:22|he told it to his two brethren|nuntiavit duobus fratribus suis]]: that is, he provoked both the rest of the Jews and the Gentiles, who were their brethren by nature, to mock Christ, saying: [[Matt 27:42|He saved others: himself he cannot save|Alios salvos fecit, se ipsum non potest salvum facere]] [the margin note here is unread; the same words stand in Mark 15:31]. And again: [[Luke 23:5|He stirreth up the people|Commovit populum]] and led them astray. [[9:23|But Sem and Japheth put a cloak upon their shoulders|At vero Sem et Japhet pallium imposuerunt humeris suis]]: that is, those converted to Christ from Judaism and from paganism reasonably excused this nakedness of Christ, and defended it from all the scorn of unbelievers, saying that Christ was made flesh and crucified not of necessity nor through any fault of his own, but out of charity and for the salvation of the whole world. Hence, according to Augustine, by the cloak is signified the sacrament [that is, the mystery], and by the shoulders the memory of things past.

paras.t: Evigilans autem Noe ex vino, hoc est, a somno mortis resurgens, quum didicisset, secundum animam a Verbo æterno, a quo tota sua humana fluxit cognitio, quæ fecerat ei filius suus minor, id est, qualiter subsannatus erat a viliori et recentiori populo Judæorum incredulo, de quibus per Isaiam locutus est, Filios enutrivi et exaltavi, ipsi autem spreverunt me; ait: Maledictus puer Chanaan, id est puerilis et stolidus populus iste incredulus, servus servorum erit fratribus suis, id est, in captivitatem et servitutem fidelium redigetur, sicut dudum impletum est.
paras.en: [[9:24|And Noe awaking from the wine|Evigilans autem Noe ex vino]], that is, rising from the sleep of death, [[9:24|when he had learned|quum didicisset]], according to his soul, from the eternal Word, from whom all his human knowledge flowed, [[9:24|what his younger son had done to him|quæ fecerat ei filius suus minor]], that is, how he had been derided by the baser and later unbelieving people of the Jews, of whom he spoke through Isaias: [[Is 1:2|I have brought up children, and exalted them: but they have despised me|Filios enutrivi et exaltavi, ipsi autem spreverunt me]]; [[9:25|He said|ait]]: [[9:25|Cursed be Chanaan|Maledictus puer Chanaan]] [Denis reads *Maledictus puer Chanaan*, "Cursed be the boy Chanaan", whence *puerilis* below], that is, this childish and foolish unbelieving people, [[9:25|a servant of servants shall he be unto his brethren|servus servorum erit fratribus suis]], that is, it shall be brought into captivity and servitude to the faithful, as was long since fulfilled.

paras.t: Porro Sem et Japhet, videlicet conversi ex Synagoga et gentibus, sunt benedicti a Deo. Dilatet Deus Japhet, id est, conversa gentilitas, per quatuor mundi partes dilatetur ac diffundatur. Et habitet in tabernaculis Sem. Hoc Rabbi Paulus exponit de Deo et Virgine gloriosa ex Sem nata, in cujus sacratissimæ Virginis mundissimo utero Unigenitus Patris per Incarnationis mysterium novem mensibus habitavit. Unde de ipsa exponitur et cantatur illud Ecclesiastici: Qui creavit me, requievit in tabernaculo meo. Japhet quoque, id est conversa gentilitas, habitavit in tabernaculis Sem, sicut præcedenti articulo patuit, et hoc de quibusdam de Sem natis, inde expulsis, puta incredulis, aliis vero permanentibus in tabernaculis illis: quia ex duobus populis illis facta est una Ecclesia. Per quod concordatur contrarietas, quæ esse videtur inter Hieronymum, asserentem quod Japhet seu gentilitas credens in Christum, habitat in tabernaculis Sem, Israele inde ejecto; et Rabbi Paulum, dicentem quod debeat intelligi, Israele non ejecto.
paras.en: But Sem and Japhet, namely those converted from the Synagogue and from the nations, are blessed by God. [[9:27|May God enlarge Japheth|Dilatet Deus Japhet]]: that is, may the converted Gentile world be enlarged and spread through the four parts of the world. [[9:27|and may he dwell in the tents of Sem|Et habitet in tabernaculis Sem]]. This Rabbi Paul [that is, Paul of Burgos, the converted rabbi who wrote Additions to Lyra] expounds of God and of the glorious Virgin born of Sem, in the most pure womb of which most holy Virgin the Only-begotten of the Father dwelt nine months through the mystery of the Incarnation. Hence that word of Ecclesiasticus is expounded and sung of her: [[Ecclus 24:12|he that made me, rested in my tabernacle|Qui creavit me, requievit in tabernaculo meo]]. Japhet too, that is, the converted Gentile world, has dwelt in the tents of Sem, as was shown in the preceding article; and this with some of those born of Sem driven out from there, namely the unbelievers, but others remaining in those tents: for of those two peoples one Church was made. By this is reconciled the contradiction that seems to stand between Jerome, who asserts that Japhet, or the Gentile world believing in Christ, dwells in the tents of Sem with Israel cast out of them, and Rabbi Paul, who says that it should be understood with Israel not cast out.

paras.t: Præterea juxta tropologiam, per Noe qui cœpit exercere terram, plantavitque vineam, designatur prælatus, gregem sibi commissum per disciplinam exercens, et verbis ac factis ædificans: qui vino inebriatur ac dormit, quando de sua prælatione aut fructificatione inaniter gloriatur, aut intumescit, aut aliqua carnalitate fœdatur, tuncque verenda, id est turpia vitia ejus nudantur. Quo cognito, Cham, id est quicumque subditus, pravus, ingratus ac indiscretus, prælatum suum dijudicat et contemnit, et fratribus seu aliis subditis, verenda patris sui ostendit, eis insinuando quod in superiore exstat culpabile; propter hoc maledictionem meretur. Sed boni subditi, talia pie quantum valent, excusant ac celant, sive dissimulant: ideo benedicuntur a Domino, atque per bona opera, seu aliorum conversionem dilatantur, ac Deo in ipsis commorante lætantur.
paras.en: Moreover, according to the tropological sense [that is, the moral sense, concerning conduct], by Noe, who began to till the ground and planted a vineyard, is signified the prelate, who exercises the flock committed to him through discipline, and edifies it by word and deed: who is drunk with wine and sleeps when he glories vainly in his prelacy or his fruitfulness, or swells with pride, or is defiled by some carnal sin; and then his nakedness, that is, his shameful vices, are laid bare. When this is known, Cham, that is, any subject who is wicked, ungrateful and indiscreet, judges and despises his prelate, and shows the nakedness of his father to his brethren, or other subjects, hinting to them what is blameworthy in their superior; and for this he deserves a curse. But good subjects excuse and cover such things dutifully, as far as they can, or pass them over in silence: therefore they are blessed by the Lord, and are enlarged through good works or through the conversion of others, and rejoice in God dwelling in them.

paras.t: Juxta hoc quæri potest, an subditi debeant superiorum suorum vitia occultare. Circa hoc in Decreto multæ inducuntur auctoritates ad partem utramque. Alexander quoque de Hales doctor præcipuus, super tertium Sententiarum multa circa hoc scribit. Sed breviter responsio stat in hoc, quod subditi non debent superiorum suorum culpas ex aliqua prava radice manifestare, nec obloqui illis, neque temerarie judicare de ipsis: sed loco et tempore opportuno, possunt ac debent illos caritative cum timore Dei et reverentia accusare apud eos, qui possunt prodesse et maxime quando commune bonum id exigit. Per hanc responsionem concordantur plurimæ auctoritates.
paras.en: In this connexion it may be asked whether subjects ought to hide the vices of their superiors. On this many authorities are brought forward in the Decretum [Gratian's collection of canon law] on either side. Alexander of Hales too, a distinguished doctor, writes much on this in his commentary on the third book of the Sentences. But in brief the answer is this: subjects must not make known the faults of their superiors out of any evil root, nor speak against them, nor judge them rashly; but in a fitting place and at a fitting time they may and must accuse them charitably, with the fear of God and with reverence, before those who are able to help, and above all when the common good requires it. By this answer very many authorities are reconciled.

10.title: Explanatio litteralis capituli decimi Genesis: Hæ sunt generationes filiorum Noe, Sem, Cham, et Japhet
10.title_en: Literal explanation of the tenth chapter of Genesis: These are the generations of the sons of Noe, Sem, Cham, and Japheth

paras.t: Nunc describuntur generationes filiorum Noe : Hæ sunt generationes filiorum Noe, videlicet istorum, Sem, Cham, et Japhet. Natique sunt eis filii post diluvium. Filii Japhet. Primo describitur generatio ipsius Japhet, qui secundum Augustinum aliosque communiter, fuit junior aliis duobus, ut gradatim ascendendo, perveniatur ad descriptionem filiorum Sem. Cujus generationem Moyses magis prosequi intendebat, quia ex eo sunt nati Hebræi.
paras.en: Now the generations of the sons of Noe are described: [[10:1|These are the generations of the sons of Noe|Hæ sunt generationes filiorum Noe]], namely of these, [[10:1|Sem, Cham, and Japheth|Sem, Cham, et Japhet]]: [[10:1|and unto them sons were born after the flood|Natique sunt eis filii post diluvium]]. [[10:2|The sons of Japheth|Filii Japhet]]. First the generation of Japheth himself is described, who, according to Augustine and others commonly, was younger than the other two, so that, going up step by step, the account may come to the description of the sons of Sem, whose generation Moses meant to follow out more fully, because from him the Hebrews were born.

paras.t: Gomer, a quo secundum Josephum nati ac nominati sunt Galatæ, qui Latine Gallogræci dicuntur, a quibus juxta quosdam postea vocati sunt Gallici. Et Magog, a quo secundum Hieronymum nati sunt Scythæ, qui et Massagetæ putantur secundum Glossam. Magog tamen quandoque est nomen populi. Unde in Ezechiele et Apocalypsi multa sunt scripta de Gog et Magog. Et Madai, a quo Medi vocati sunt ; et Javan, de quo Græci descenderunt, propter quod usque nunc Græcia in Hebræo vocatur Javan ; et Thubal, de quo Hispani ; et Mosoch, de quo Cappadoces ; et Thiras, a quo Trachæi seu Thraces.
paras.en: [[10:2|Gomer|Gomer]], from whom, according to Josephus, were born and named the Galatians, who in Latin are called Gallogræci [that is, Gallo-Greeks], from whom, according to some, the Gauls were afterwards named; [[10:2|and Magog|Et Magog]], from whom, according to Jerome, were born the Scythians, who are also thought to be the Massagetæ, according to the Gloss. Yet Magog is sometimes the name of a people: hence in Ezechiel[[Ezech 38:1||]][[Ezech 39:1||]] and the Apocalypse[[Apoc 20:7||]] much is written of Gog and Magog. [[10:2|and Madai|Et Madai]], from whom the Medes were named; [[10:2|and Javan|et Javan]], from whom the Greeks descended, for which reason Greece is called Javan in Hebrew to this day; [[10:2|and Thubal|et Thubal]], from whom the Spaniards; [[10:2|and Mosoch|et Mosoch]], from whom the Cappadocians; [[10:2|and Thiras|et Thiras]], from whom the Trachæi or Thracians.

paras.t: Porro filii Gomer fuerunt : Asenech, quod nomen interdum est appellatio feminæ, nam uxor Joseph vocata est Asenech ; et Riphath, et Thogorma. Filii autem Javan fuerunt : Elisa, a quo Elisæi, id est Græci ; et Tharsis, a quo Cilices, quorum urbs nomine Tharsus, a Paulo apostolo nobilis est ; Cetthim, et Dodanim, a quo Rhodii.
paras.en: [[10:3|And the sons of Gomer|Porro filii Gomer]] were: [[10:3|Ascenez|Asenech]] [Denis reads *Asenech*], which name is sometimes the name of a woman, for the wife of Joseph was called Asenech; [[10:3|and Riphath and Thogorma|et Riphath, et Thogorma]]. [[10:4|And the sons of Javan|Filii autem Javan]] were: [[10:4|Elisa|Elisa]], from whom the Elisæi, that is, the Greeks; [[10:4|and Tharsis|et Tharsis]], from whom the Cilicians, whose city, Tharsus by name, is made famous by the apostle Paul[[Acts 22:3||]]; [[10:4|Cetthim and Dodanim|Cetthim, et Dodanim]], from whom the Rhodians.

paras.t: Ab his divisæ sunt insulæ gentium in regionibus suis, id est, a præfatis filiis atque nepotibus Japhet facta est insularum aliquarum partitio, unaquaque tribu appropriante sibi provinciam aliquam. Ideo subditur : Unusquisque secundum linguam suam et familias suas in nationibus suis, hoc est, quilibet sortitus est mansionem in terra populi sui et linguæ suæ, quod tamen post dissipationem turris Babylonicæ factum est, et nunc per anticipationem narratur, quoniam usque ad turris illius constructionem una omnium fuit lingua.
paras.en: [[10:5|By these were divided the islands of the Gentiles in their lands|Ab his divisæ sunt insulæ gentium in regionibus suis]], that is, by the aforesaid sons and grandsons of Japheth a partition of certain islands was made, each tribe appropriating some province to itself. Therefore it is added: [[10:5|every one according to his tongue and their families in their nations|Unusquisque secundum linguam suam et familias suas in nationibus suis]], that is, each one received by lot a dwelling in the land of his own people and his own tongue. This, however, took place after the tower of Babylon was overthrown, and is told here by anticipation, since until the building of that tower all had one tongue.

paras.t: Deinde describitur generatio Cham, qui medius fuit inter filios Noe. Filii autem Cham fuerunt : Chus, a quo Æthiopes : hinc Æthiopia in Hebræo Chus nominatur ; et Mesraim, a quo descenderunt Ægyptii : nam et Ægyptus in Hebræo Mesraim nuncupatur ; et Phuth, de quo Libyes, qui post Phuthæi vocati sunt : unde fluvius Mauritaniæ Phuth dicitur, et omnis regio ista vocatur Phuthensis, secundum Glossam ; et Chanaan, de quo nati sunt Chananæi. Filii autem Chus fuerunt : Saba, a quo Sabæi ; et Hevila, de quo Gætuli, in parte majoris Africæ adhærentes deserto : et Sabatha, de quo Sabatheni, qui et Astabori dicuntur, secundum Hieronymum ; et Regma, et Sabathaca. Filii Regma filii Chus, nati ex Cham : Saba, et Dadan. Secundum Hieronymum, Regma et Sabathaca perdiderunt paulatim nomina sua antiqua, et quæ nomina habeant nunc pro illis ignoratur.
paras.en: Next the generation of Cham is described, who was the middle one among the sons of Noe. [[10:6|And the Sons of Cham|Filii autem Cham]] were: [[10:6|Chus|Chus]], from whom the Ethiopians: hence Ethiopia is named Chus in Hebrew; [[10:6|and Mesram|et Mesraim]], from whom the Egyptians descended, for Egypt too is called Mesraim in Hebrew; [[10:6|and Phuth|et Phuth]], from whom the Libyans, who were afterwards called Phuthæans: hence a river of Mauritania is called Phuth, and that whole region is called Phuthensis, according to the Gloss; [[10:6|and Chanaan|et Chanaan]], from whom the Chanaanites were born. [[10:7|And the sons of Chus|Filii autem Chus]] were: [[10:7|Saba|Saba]], from whom the Sabæans; [[10:7|and Hevila|et Hevila]], from whom the Getulians, who border on the desert in a part of greater Africa; [[10:7|and Sabatha|et Sabatha]], from whom the Sabatheni, who are also called Astabori, according to Jerome; [[10:7|and Regma, and Sabatacha|et Regma, et Sabathaca]]. [[10:7|The sons of Regma|Filii Regma]], the son of Chus, born of Cham: [[10:7|Saba, and Dadan|Saba, et Dadan]]. According to Jerome, Regma and Sabathaca little by little lost their ancient names, and what names they now have in their stead is not known.

paras.t: Porro Chus genuit Nemrod. Ex hoc rursus suspectus est libellus Methodii, in quo Nemrod dicitur natus de filiis Hiron filii Sem. Et quamvis Nemrod regnasset super posteros Cham ex hoc non diceretur natus de Chus filio Cham. Ipse cœpit esse potens in terra. Unde Septuaginta transtulerunt. Cœpit esse gigas in terra, atque ut fertur in glossa Scholasticæ historiæ, decem cubitorum exstiterat.
paras.en: [[10:8|Now Chus begot Nemrod|Porro Chus genuit Nemrod]]. From this, again, the little book of Methodius is suspect, in which Nemrod is said to have been born of the sons of Hiron, the son of Sem. And even if Nemrod had reigned over the descendants of Cham, he would not on that account be said to be born of Chus, the son of Cham. [[10:8|he began to be mighty on the earth|Ipse cœpit esse potens in terra]]. Here the Septuagint translated: He began to be a giant on the earth; and, as is said in a gloss on the Scholastic History, he was ten cubits tall.

paras.t: Et erat robustus venator coram Domino. Circa hoc loquitur Alcuinus : Nemrod fuit robustus venator, id est hominum oppressor atque exstinctor, allexitque homines ad ædificandum Babylonicam turrim. Josephus quoque ait : Nemrod nova cupiditate regnandi tyrannidem arripuit, fuitque auctor ædificandæ turris quæ tangeret cœlum. Fuit itaque fortis venator coram Domino qui omnia intuetur. Tamen secundum Augustinum melius dicitur, quod fuit fortis venator contra Dominum, id est Deo per superbiam suam contrarius ac rebellis. Sicque habet translatio qua utitur Augustinus. Credo etiam quod fuit bestiarum venator, quemadmodum Lamech ante diluvium, non tamen solum propter animalium pelles ut Lamech, sed item propter carnes bestiarum edendas. Ab hoc excrevit proverbium : Quasi Nemrod robustus venator coram Domino : id est, quando aliquis videbatur magnus tyrannus, validusque oppressor sive venator, dicebatur de eo verbum istud vulgare : Iste quasi Nemrod robustus venator coram Domino.
paras.en: [[10:9|And he was a stout hunter before the Lord|Et erat robustus venator coram Domino]]. On this Alcuin says: Nemrod was a stout hunter, that is, an oppressor and destroyer of men, and he enticed men to build the tower of Babylon. Josephus also says: Nemrod, from a new lust for ruling, seized a tyranny, and was the author of the building of a tower that should touch heaven. So he was a strong hunter before the Lord, who beholds all things. Yet according to Augustine it is better said that he was a strong hunter against the Lord, that is, contrary and rebellious to God through his pride; and so has the translation which Augustine uses. I believe, too, that he was a hunter of beasts, as Lamech was before the flood, yet not only for the skins of the animals, as Lamech was, but also for the flesh of the beasts, to eat it. [[10:9|Hence came a proverb|Ab hoc excrevit proverbium]] [the edition's margin gives the variant *Ob hoc*, 'for this reason', as the Vulgate reads]: [[10:9|Even as Nemrod the stout hunter before the Lord|Quasi Nemrod robustus venator coram Domino]]; that is, when anyone seemed a great tyrant and a mighty oppressor or hunter, this common saying was said of him: This man is like Nemrod the stout hunter before the Lord.

paras.t: Fuit autem principium regni ejus Babylon, id est, Nemrod primo regnare incepit in Babylone, quæ tamen tunc aliter vocabatur : nam propter divisionem linguarum, ibi postea factam, dicta est Babylon ; et Arach, id est Edessa civitas Mesopotamiæ alio nomine, et Achad, et Chalanne, quæ postea a Seleuco rege Asiæ, Seleucia est vocata. Regnavit ergo in urbibus istis, in terra, id est regione Sennaar.
paras.en: [[10:10|And the beginning of his kingdom was Babylon|Fuit autem principium regni ejus Babylon]], that is, Nemrod first began to reign in Babylon, which, however, was then called otherwise: for it was called Babylon on account of the division of tongues made there afterwards [Babylon, in Hebrew *Babel*, being taken to mean confusion]; [[10:10|and Arach|et Arach]], that is, by another name Edessa, a city of Mesopotamia; [[10:10|and Achad, and Chalanne|et Achad, et Chalanne]], which was afterwards called Seleucia by Seleucus, king of Asia. He reigned, then, in these cities, [[10:10|in the land|in terra]], that is, in the region, [[10:10|of Sennaar|Sennaar]].

paras.t: De terra illa, videlicet Sennaar, egressus est Assur. Hoc quidam exponunt de Assur filio Sem, dicentes quod Assur iste noluit acquiescere impio Nemrod in ædificatione turris, idcirco recessit et fugit ab eo ad terram remotam ante inhabitatam, quæ post ex nomine ejus est vocata Assyria. In Scholastica quoque historia dicitur, quod Nemrod violenter expulit illum Assur de terra Sennaar, quæ ejus erat hereditario jure. Quidam vero exponunt istud non de Assur filio Sem, sed de regno Assyriorum, quod dicunt inde egressum. Sed primæ expositioni videtur concordare, quod subditur : Et ædificavit Niniven, et plateas civitatis illius, et Chale, id est urbem sic dictam. Resen quoque urbem sitam inter Niniven et Chale. Hæc, scilicet Ninive, est civitas magna. Scriptum est enim in Jona : Ninive magna erat itinere dierum trium. Ubi Hieronymus ait, quod tanta fuit magnitudo ipsius, quantum ad murorum circuitum, imo secundum Glossam ibidem, circuiri vix poterat infra tres dies. Denique Augustinus scribit de his, quod Assur dicitur exisse de terra Sennaar, ædificasseque Niniven ac alias urbes, longe postea factum est : quod Moyses hac occasione perstrinxit, ut nobilitatem regni Assyriorum ostenderet, quod Ninus filius Beli dilatavit mirifice, conditor civitatis quæ ex nomine ejus vocata est Ninive. Veruntamen alii dicunt, quod præfatus Assur filius Sem, condidit Niniven, tamen sub alio nomine, postmodum vero vocata est Ninive a Nino, qui eam plurimum ampliavit.
paras.en: [[10:11|Out of that land|De terra illa]], namely Sennaar, [[10:11|came forth Assur|egressus est Assur]]. Some explain this of Assur the son of Sem, saying that this Assur would not go along with the wicked Nemrod in the building of the tower, and therefore withdrew and fled from him to a distant land not inhabited before, which was afterwards called Assyria after his name. In the Scholastic History too it is said that Nemrod drove that Assur by force out of the land of Sennaar, which was his by right of inheritance. Others, however, explain it not of Assur the son of Sem but of the kingdom of the Assyrians, which they say went forth from there. But what follows seems to agree with the first explanation: [[10:11|and built Ninive, and the streets of the city|Et ædificavit Niniven, et plateas civitatis illius]], [[10:11|and Chale|et Chale]], that is, a city so called. [[10:12|Resen also|Resen quoque]], a city lying [[10:12|between Ninive and Chale|inter Niniven et Chale]]; [[10:12|this|Hæc]], namely Ninive, [[10:12|is the great city|est civitas magna]]. For it is written in Jonas: [[Jon 3:3|Ninive was a great city of three days' journey|Ninive magna erat itinere dierum trium]]. On which Jerome says that its size was so great with respect to the circuit of its walls; nay rather, according to the Gloss on the same place, it could scarcely be gone round within three days. Lastly, Augustine writes of these things that Assur's being said to have gone out of the land of Sennaar and to have built Ninive and other cities happened long afterwards: Moses touched on it here to show the renown of the kingdom of the Assyrians, which Ninus, the son of Belus, wonderfully enlarged, the founder of the city that was called Ninive after his name. Others, however, say that the aforesaid Assur, the son of Sem, founded Ninive, though under another name, and that it was afterwards called Ninive from Ninus, who greatly enlarged it.

paras.t: At vero Mesraim, filius Cham, genuit Ludim, et Anamim, et Laabim, etc. Ponuntur hic nomina filiorum Mesraim, per quæ septem gentes ex illis filiis natæ insinuantur ; atque ut ait Hieronymus, gentes istæ ignotæ sunt nobis, vel quia præliis sunt deletæ, aut alia nomina sunt sortitæ, excepto Laabim, a quo dicti sunt Libyes, qui ante vocabantur Phuthæi. Et Chasluim ; de quibus egressi, id est nati sunt Philistiim et Caphtorim.
paras.en: [[10:13|And Mesraim|At vero Mesraim]], the son of Cham, [[10:13|begot Ludim, and Anamim and Laabim|genuit Ludim, et Anamim, et Laabim]], etc. The names of the sons of Mesraim are set down here, by which are indicated seven peoples born of those sons; and, as Jerome says, these peoples are unknown to us, either because they were wiped out in wars or because they received other names, except Laabim, from whom the Libyans were named, who before were called Phuthæans. [[10:14|and Chasluim; of whom came forth|Et Chasluim ; de quibus egressi]], that is, were born, [[10:14|the Philistines, and the Capthorim|sunt Philistiim et Caphtorim]].

paras.t: Porro circa illud quod dictum est, Filii Regma, Saba et Dadan, Josephus dicit : Filii Regma, Saba et Judas. Et dicit quod Judas iste in Ægypto habitans, Judæis cognomen suum reliquit, ita quod ab eo Judæi sunt dicti. Quod non videtur idonee dictum, quia etsi filius iste Regma dictus fuerit Judas, tamen de semine fuit Cham : ideo non apparet, quod Judæi de Sem nati, ab isto Juda Cham filio, cognomen acceperint : sed potius a Juda patriarcha filio Jacob, qui inter fratres suos fuit fortissimus, atque post Joseph præcipuus, quia ex eo nati sunt reges.
paras.en: Now concerning what was said, [[10:7|The sons of Regma: Saba, and Dadan|Filii Regma, Saba et Dadan]], Josephus says: The sons of Regma, Saba and Judas. And he says that this Judas, dwelling in Egypt, left his name to the Jews, so that the Jews were called after him. This does not seem fitly said: for even if this son of Regma was called Judas, still he was of the seed of Cham; so it does not appear that the Jews, born of Sem, took their name from this Judas, a son of Cham, but rather from Juda the patriarch, the son of Jacob, who was the strongest among his brethren[[Gen 49:8||]] and the chief after Joseph, because kings were born of him.

paras.t: Deinceps ponuntur nomina filiorum Chanaan. Chanaan autem genuit Sidonem primogenitum suum, a quo nominata est Sidon urbs Phœniciæ ; et Hethæum et Jebusæum et Amorrhæum et Gergesæum et Hevæum : omnia ista propria nomina, etiam sunt nomina communia populorum ex viris natorum, ut infra in multis patebit locis : et Aracæum, qui construxit oppidum nomine Arcas, contra Tripolim in radicibus Libani : et Cynæum, a quo urbs Cyn ; et Aradium, a quo Aradii, qui Aradiam insulam inhabitaverunt : Samaræum, a quo Samaria nomen sumpsit : et Amathæum, a quo Emath civitas, quæ alio nomine Antiochia appellatur. Et per hos disseminati sunt populi Chananæorum, id est, diversæ gentes, videlicet undecim, natæ et multiplicatæ sunt super terram ex undecim fratribus illis.
paras.en: Next are set down the names of the sons of Chanaan. [[10:15|And Chanaan begot Sidon his firstborn|Chanaan autem genuit Sidonem primogenitum suum]], from whom Sidon, a city of Phœnicia, was named; [[10:15|the Hethite|et Hethæum]], [[10:16|And the Jebusite, and the Amorrhite, and the Gergesite|et Jebusæum et Amorrhæum et Gergesæum]], [[10:17|The Hevite|et Hevæum]]: all these proper names are also the common names of the peoples born of these men, as will appear below in many places; [[10:17|and Aracite|et Aracæum]], who built a town named Arcas, over against Tripolis, at the foot of Libanus; [[10:17|the Sinite|et Cynæum]] [Denis reads *Cynæum*; the edition's margin gives *Sinæum*, as the Vulgate has it], from whom the city of Cyn; [[10:18|And the Aradian|et Aradium]], from whom the Aradians, who inhabited the island of Aradus; [[10:18|the Samarite|Samaræum]], from whom Samaria took its name; [[10:18|and the Hamathite|et Amathæum]], from whom Emath, a city which by another name is called Antioch. [[10:18|and afterwards the families of the Chanaanites were spread abroad|Et per hos disseminati sunt populi Chananæorum]] [Denis reads *per hos*, 'through these', where the Vulgate has *post hæc*, 'afterwards'], that is, various peoples, namely eleven, were born and multiplied over the earth from those eleven brothers.

paras.t: Factique sunt termini Chanaan venientibus a Sidone Geraram usque Gazam : id est, loca habitationis gentium harum extendebantur a civitate Sidone, ambulantibus ibi usque Geraram Palæstinæ, et Gazam urbem Philistiim ; donec ingrediaris Sodomam et Gomorrham et Adamam et Seboim, id est terram ubi quatuor urbes istæ stabant, antequam subverterentur igne et sulfure : quæ et subversæ erant, quando hæc Moyses scripsit : non tamen, quando quæ narrat nunc, contigerunt. Hi sunt filii Cham : hoc est generati ab eo, non immediate, sed per Chanaan.
paras.en: [[10:19|And the limits of Chanaan were from Sidon as one comes to Gerara even to Gaza|Factique sunt termini Chanaan venientibus a Sidone Geraram usque Gazam]], that is, the places where these peoples dwelt stretched from the city of Sidon, for those travelling that way, as far as Gerara in Palestine and Gaza, a city of the Philistines; [[10:19|until thou enter Sodom and Gomorrha, and Adama, and Seboim|donec ingrediaris Sodomam et Gomorrham et Adamam et Seboim]] [the edition's margin adds *usque Lesa*, 'even to Lesa', as the Vulgate reads], that is, the land where these four cities stood before they were overthrown by fire and brimstone: they had indeed been overthrown when Moses wrote these things, but not when the things he now tells came to pass. [[10:20|These are the children of Cham|Hi sunt filii Cham]], that is, begotten by him, not immediately but through Chanaan.

paras.t: Consequenter describitur generatio Sem, quæ ultimo enarratur, quoniam Moyses vult eam diffusius prosequi. De Sem quoque nati sunt patres filiorum omnium Heber, hoc est, patres omnium qui nati sunt ex Heber, geniti sunt ex Sem : ita quod universi Hebræi sunt nati de semine Sem. Et specialiter exprimit ipsum Heber, quamvis sit quintus a Sem, quia ex Heber nati ac cognominati sunt Hebræi, in quibus viguit cultus Dei, quibus et Moyses scripsit hæc. Fratre Japhet majore : qui Sem fuit major seu senior ac dignior fratre suo Japhet.
paras.en: Next the generation of Sem is described, which is told last because Moses means to follow it out more fully. [[10:21|Of Sem also|De Sem quoque]] were born the fathers [[10:21|of all the children of Heber|filiorum omnium Heber]] [Denis reads *patres*, 'the fathers'; the edition's margin gives *patre*, 'the father', as the Vulgate has it], that is, the fathers of all who were born of Heber were begotten of Sem, so that all the Hebrews were born of the seed of Sem. And he names Heber himself in particular, although he is the fifth from Sem, because from Heber were born and named the Hebrews, among whom the worship of God flourished, and for whom Moses wrote these things. [[10:21|the elder brother of Japheth|Fratre Japhet majore]]: for Sem was greater, that is, older, and worthier than his brother Japheth.

paras.t: Filii Sem fuerunt : Elam, a quo descenderunt Elamitæ ac principes Persidis : et Assur, a quo Assyrii : et Arphaxad, a quo Chaldæi : et Lud, a quo Lydii : et Aram, a quo Syri, quorum metropolis est Damascus. Filii Aram fuerunt : Hus, qui condidit Trachonitidem et Damascum, secundum Glossam, et dominatus est ibi, a quo etiam nominata est terra Hus, quam Septuaginta Ausitidem vocant, id est australem. Unde in libro Job, ubi nostra habet translatio, Vir erat in terra Hus : Septuaginta transtulerunt, Vir fuit in terra Ausitidis. De semine Hus creditur Job fuisse, juxta Scripturam prætactam : Vir erat in terra Hus, nomine Job. Et Hul, a quo Armenii, qui ab Euphrate fluvio tenent Asiæ partem usque ad Indicum mare : et Gether, a quo Acharii : et Mes, a quo Messii, qui a Septuaginta vocantur Mosoch, id est Mæones.
paras.en: [[10:22|The sons of Sem|Filii Sem]] were: [[10:22|Elam|Elam]], from whom descended the Elamites and the princes of Persia; [[10:22|and Assur|et Assur]], from whom the Assyrians; [[10:22|and Arphaxad|et Arphaxad]], from whom the Chaldeans; [[10:22|and Lud|et Lud]], from whom the Lydians; [[10:22|and Aram|et Aram]], from whom the Syrians, whose chief city is Damascus. [[10:23|The sons of Aram|Filii Aram]] were: [[10:23|Us|Hus]] [Denis reads *Hus*, as in the book of Job], who founded Trachonitis and Damascus, according to the Gloss, and ruled there; from whom the land of Hus too was named, which the Septuagint calls Ausitis, that is, the southern land. Hence in the book of Job, where our translation has [[Job 1:1|There was a man in the land of Hus|Vir erat in terra Hus]], the Septuagint translated: There was a man in the land of Ausitis. Job is believed to have been of the seed of Hus, according to the Scripture just touched on: [[Job 1:1|There was a man in the land of Hus, whose name was Job|Vir erat in terra Hus, nomine Job]]. [[10:23|and Hull|Et Hul]], from whom the Armenians, who hold the part of Asia from the river Euphrates as far as the Indian sea; [[10:23|and Gether|et Gether]], from whom the Acharii; [[10:23|and Mes|et Mes]], from whom the Messii, who by the Septuagint are called Mosoch, that is, the Mæonians.

paras.t: At vero Arphaxad genuit Sale, de quo ortus est Heber. Natique sunt Heber filii duo. Nomen uni Phaleg, id est quod interpretatur divisio, ideo subditur ratio nominis ejus : eo quod in diebus ejus divisa sit terra : quia in tempore ejus creditur facta linguarum confusio, destructio turris, et ex consequenti provinciarum distinctio. Dicuntque aliqui, quod Heber hoc prævidit in spiritu, tanquam prophetiæ spiritum habens, idcirco filium suum sic appellavit. Et nomen fratris ejus Jectan.
paras.en: [[10:24|But Arphaxad begot Sale, of whom was born Heber|At vero Arphaxad genuit Sale, de quo ortus est Heber]]. [[10:25|And to Heber were born two sons|Natique sunt Heber filii duo]]: [[10:25|the name of the one was Phaleg|Nomen uni Phaleg]], that is, a name which means division; therefore the reason for his name is added: [[10:25|because in his days was the earth divided|eo quod in diebus ejus divisa sit terra]]; for in his time, it is believed, the confusion of tongues took place, the destruction of the tower, and in consequence the distinguishing of the provinces. And some say that Heber foresaw this in spirit, as having the spirit of prophecy, and therefore so named his son. [[10:25|and his brother's name Jectan|Et nomen fratris ejus Jectan]].

paras.t: Qui Jectan genuit Elmodad, et alios undecim qui nominantur in textu : et populi nati ex eis, sunt nobis ignoti, secundum Hieronymum, ex causis prætactis.
paras.en: [[10:26|Which Jectan begot Elmodad|Qui Jectan genuit Elmodad]], and eleven others who are named in the text [the text in fact names twelve more]; and the peoples born of them are unknown to us, according to Jerome, for the reasons touched on above.

paras.t: Hæ familiæ Noe, juxta populos et nationes suas, id est secundum numerum et distinctionem ipsorum. Ab his divisæ sunt penitus in terra post diluvium. Dicit autem Isidorus, quod ex tribus filiis Noe natæ sunt gentes septuaginta duæ, videlicet quindecim de Japhet, triginta de Cham, viginti septem de Sem. Idem in Scholastica historia refertur. Verumtamen Augustinus computat ex eis generationes seu tribus ac gentes septuaginta tres. De Cham enim computat nationes triginta et unam. Nihilo minus Augustinus post fatetur, quod melius computantur non nisi septuaginta duæ. Non est autem putandum, secundum Augustinum, quod non fuerint multo plures homines nati ex præfatis filiis trium filiorum Noe, quam in littera ista exprimitur.
paras.en: [[10:32|These are the families of Noe, according to their people and nations|Hæ familiæ Noe, juxta populos et nationes suas]], that is, according to their number and distinction. [[10:32|By these were the nations divided on the earth after the flood|Ab his divisæ sunt penitus in terra post diluvium]]. Now Isidore says that from the three sons of Noe were born seventy-two peoples: fifteen from Japheth, thirty from Cham, twenty-seven from Sem. The same is related in the Scholastic History. Augustine, however, counts from them seventy-three generations, or tribes and peoples, for from Cham he counts thirty-one nations. Nevertheless Augustine afterwards admits that they are better counted as no more than seventy-two. But, according to Augustine, it is not to be thought that there were not many more men born of the aforesaid sons of the three sons of Noe than are expressed in this text.

paras.t: Præterea Alcuinus ait: Sem, ut adstruunt, sortitus est Asiam, Cham Africam, Japhet Europam. Unde Josephus ait apertius: Filii Japhet tenuerunt septentrionalem regionem, a Tauro et Amano montibus Ciliciæ et Syriæ usque ad fluvium Tanaim; in Europa vero usque ad Gadira. Filii vero Cham a provincia Syriæ, et Amano et Libano montibus, cunctas terras obtinuerunt, quæcumque ad mare sunt positæ, appendentes etiam eas quæ sunt usque Oceanum. Filii vero Sem seorsum habitaverunt, ab Euphrate facientes initium.
paras.en: Further, Alcuin says: Sem, as they maintain, received Asia by lot, Cham Africa, Japheth Europe.
